title: Harmonize dataset ingestion and eval-runner synthesis for reproducible profile publishing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Model onboarding and profile publishing pipelines suffer from subtle nondeterminism across three layers: dataset ingestion (different sampling & normalizations), prompt variant expansion (tokenization and whitespace differences), and eval runner execution (timeout/parallelism variability). This makes it difficult to pin a model version to a stable 'performance profile' that is reproducible across environments.

Goal: Create a harmonized curation + runner synthesis flow that guarantees reproducible profile artifacts (manifests, checksums, and deterministic seedbanks) and integrates cleanly with version pinning so downstream serving and rollouts can rely on stable published profiles. Deliver an end-to-end CI gated pipeline for profile publishing with clear observability and rollback hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dataset ingestion produces canonical shards and a dataset manifest with stable checksums across runs (same input -> same manifest).
2) Prompt expansion is deterministic: tokenizer/version recorded, canonical whitespace rules applied, prompt-variant mapping produced.
3) Eval runners run in a synthesis mode that pins seeds, worker counts, and time budgets and emits reproducible run metadata.
4) Profile publisher composes dataset+prompt+runner artifacts into a single profile bundle with manifest.json and content-addressed artifact URIs.
5) CI gates verify artifact checksums and run a lightweight smoke eval comparing key metrics to previous profile; differences above threshold block publishing.
6) Profiles are discoverable in the registry and can be referenced from model pinning configs (e.g., model: v1.3 + profile: profile-2026-03-14).
design_notes:
- Prefer simple, auditable transforms in ingestion rather than complex heuristics; keep raw ingest as upload-only and produce a canonicalized layer for benchmarking.
- Trade-off: full dedupe/normalization will increase ingestion time/cost but is necessary for reproducibility; we will implement as an optional pipeline flag for initial rollout.
- Prompt expansion will embed tokenizer metadata (tokenizer name + version + vocab checksum) to avoid silent drift.
- Runner synthesis will run both a fast, deterministic pass (single-threaded, seed pinned) and an optional production-like pass (parallelism for throughput signals). Only deterministic pass is considered authoritative for profile publishing.
- Backwards compatibility: published profiles include a 'compatibility' field listing minimal runtime features required (KV-cache schema, max-seq, quantization support).
technical_plan:
1) Ingestion: implement canonicalizer service that normalizes text, dedupes near-duplicates (configurable threshold), shards deterministically, and outputs a manifest with SHA256 checksums for each shard. Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canonical+Dataset+Spec.
2) Prompts: add an expansion step that records tokenizer metadata and produces a canonicalized prompt file; add unit tests that round-trip tokenization across supported tokenizers.
3) Runner shim: implement a 'synthesis' flag in the harness which forces deterministic scheduling, a fixed RNG seed (seedbank), fixed worker_count=1 for the authoritative run, and time-budget enforcement. PR skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/1372.
4) Profile composer: a microservice (profile-publisher) that assembles artifacts into profile bundles, computes content-addressed URIs (CAS), validates checksums, and posts to the profile registry. Store bundles in artifacts bucket under /profiles/{model}/{profile-id}/.
5) CI/Release: integrate smoke-compare job in GitHub Actions; small delta thresholds stored in runtime-config. Publishing requires 2 approvals (PM + Bench Eng).
6) Observability: emit profiling telemetry (p50/p95 latency, token cost, GPU-steps) and attach to profile metadata. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/profiles.
7) Documentation: onboarding playbook (Confluence) + sample pinning config in examples repo.

Milestones: M1 canonicalizer + prompt expansion (2w), M2 runner synthesis flag + seedbank (2w), M3 profile composer + CI gating (1w), M4 rollout & docs (1w).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Determinism breaks if tokenizer or model binaries are updated; Mitigation: record tokenizer/model runtime checksums and fail publish if mismatch.
- Risk: Canonicalization causes data loss for some datasets; Mitigation: keep raw ingest snapshots and provide a 'do-not-canonicalize' opt-in label for sensitive datasets.
- Risk: Publishing pipeline becomes bottleneck; Mitigation: composer does content-addressing and dedup to reduce storage and will support streaming uploads.
- Risk: CI false-positives for metric deltas; Mitigation: tune thresholds and add an explicit 're-eval in production-like mode' step before a manual override path.
